summary:
[  edit  ]
The Extrude  SOP  can be used for:
Extruding and bevelling Text and other geometry
Cusping the bevelled edges to get sharp edges
Making primitives thicker or thinner
The default is a 1 unit extrusion directly backwards from the input geometry's normals.
It uses the normal of the surface to determine the direction of extrusion. In the case of planar or open polygons, the normal is difficult to determine, and may not always provide the result that you expect. Turn on the  Primitive  Normals display in the  Viewer  display options to see the normals.
The extrusion is created by extending surfaces from the vertices of the input geometry along the cross-section curve given in the second input (Input 1). The first vertex of the cross-section curve is placed by default at the vertices of the input geometry and aligned so that the curve's positive Y axis extends opposite to the input geometry's normal. The cross-section's positive X axis by default extends outwards from center of the input geometry.
If no cross-section curve is given, a vertical line going from (0,0,0) to (0,1,0) is used. This results in a 1 unit extrusion directly backwards from the input geometry's normals. As another example, using a straight line from (0,0,0) to (.1,.1,0) will result in an extrusion that extends 1 unit backwards from the input and flares .1 unit outwards on all sides. The Thickness and Depth parameters can be used to shift and scale the cross-section without directly changing the curve.
Note:  The shape of the cross-section is always relative to its first vertex, so shifting the entire cross-section curve will have no effect. Also, only the X and Y axes of the curve are used i.e. Z position values are ignored.
After the new geometry is created, normals are computed by default.
Warning:  If you take a default output from a  Text SOP  and Extrude it, it may have bad rendering artifacts (and too many polygons) as it's extruding each of the triangles of the triangulated letters. You need to change the Output parameter of the Text  SOP  to Closed Polygons. See  OP Snippets .

parameters.label: Fuse Points
parameters.name: dofuse
parameters.description: ⊞  - This should almost always be turned on when cross-sections are used. It consolidates points of polygons that would otherwise cross or overlap when the bevel takes place.

parameters.label: Front Face
parameters.name: fronttype
parameters.description: ⊞  - Control how the front face of the extrusion should be built. You may wish to have a "No Output" because some faces are never actually seen when doing animation and, therefore, would only take up additional overhead if left on.

parameters.label: No Output
parameters.name: off
parameters.description: No face is created.

parameters.label: Output Face
parameters.name: face
parameters.description: Faces are created.

parameters.label: Convex Face
parameters.name: convex
parameters.description: Create faces built with Convex Polygons (use this option if faces are to be deformed, i.e.  Twist SOP ,  Lattice SOP ).

parameters.label: Back Face
parameters.name: backtype
parameters.description: ⊞  - This value controls whether or not the back of the extruded object will have a face or not. The options are the same as the Front Face options above.

parameters.label: Side Mesh
parameters.name: sidetype
parameters.description: ⊞  - Controls how the cross-section(s) will be extruded. If the input cross-section is a Bzier or NURBS curve, the surface will be constructed with a patch of the same geometry type.

parameters.label: No Output
parameters.name: off
parameters.description: No mesh is created.

parameters.label: Rows
parameters.name: rows
parameters.description: Creates horizontal lines.

parameters.label: Columns
parameters.name: cols
parameters.description: Creates vertical lines.

parameters.label: Rows and Columns
parameters.name: rowcol
parameters.description: Both Rows and Columns. Looks like Quads in wire frame display, but all polygons are open (if the primitive type is polygon). Compare them in the Model Editor.

parameters.label: Triangles
parameters.name: triangles
parameters.description: Build the grid with Triangles.

parameters.label: Quadrilaterals
parameters.name: quads
parameters.description: Generates sides composed of quadrilaterals (default).

parameters.label: Alternating triangles
parameters.name: alttriangles
parameters.description: Generates triangles that are opposed; similar to the Triangles option.

parameters.label: Initialize Extrusion
parameters.name: initextrude
parameters.description: If the cross-section face that you created doesn't match up nicely to the size of the geometry you are extruding, this command will scale and translate it so that it fits nicely.

parameters.label: The reason it might not be nice to begin with is that the curve wasn't drawn exactly on the world
parameters.description: axis in Model-mode and/or was drawn at a grossly different scale than the object it is extruding.

parameters.label: Thickness Translate
parameters.name: thickxlate
parameters.description: Shifts the cross-section profile perpendicularly to the normals of the input geometry. This relates to the X axis of the cross-section profile. When used with text, this typically has the effect of making the text lighter (narrower) or heavier (bolder).

parameters.label: Thickness Scale
parameters.name: thickscale
parameters.description: Scales the cross-section profile perpendicularly to the normals of the input geometry. This is equivalent to scaling the cross-section in its X axis. This parameter has no effect on the default profile, which is equivalent to a vertical line along the Y axis. Negative scaling values are allowed.

parameters.label: Depth Translate
parameters.name: depthxlate
parameters.description: Moves the cross-section in the direction of the normal. Positive values will move backwards to the direction of the normal. Depth movement relates to the Y axis of the input cross-section. Using this parameter will shift the position of the output geometry in direction of the normal.

parameters.label: Depth Scale
parameters.name: depthscale
parameters.description: Scales the cross-section in the direction of the source geometry's normals. This is equivalent to scaling the input cross-section in its Y axis and will determine how deep (thick) the resulting extrusion is.

parameters.label: Vertex
parameters.name: vertex
parameters.description: Translates the cross-section such that the vertex specified is at the cross-section origin.

parameters.label: Cusp Polygonal Sides
parameters.name: docusp
parameters.description: Determines whether or not sides are to be smooth-shaded or faceted using the angle value in Side Cusp Angle field.

parameters.label: Cusping lets you specify at which angle between adjacent polygons, a sharp edge (faceted edge where vertices are un
parameters.description: shared) should be displayed instead.

parameters.label: Side Cusp Angle
parameters.name: cuspangle
parameters.description: When checked, this value will control the angle at which faceting of the sides will occur. A value of 20 is default.

parameters.label: Consolidate Faces to Mesh
parameters.name: sharefaces
parameters.description: If selected the extrusion will share points between the front face and the first row of the side mesh and between the last face and the last row of the side mesh.

parameters.label: Remove Shared Sides
parameters.name: removesharedsides
parameters.description: Prevents the creation of duplicate sides.

parameters.label: Create Output Groups
parameters.name: newg
parameters.description: When this option is checked, it causes the Extrude  SOP  to generate three new groups representing the primitives belonging to the front faces, back faces, and the side bevel/extrusion. The name of the groups are determined by the three option fields below.

parameters.label: Front  Group
parameters.name: frontgrp
parameters.description: Output group name to create for front face geometry.

parameters.label: Back  Group
parameters.name: backgrp
parameters.description: Output group name to create for back face geometry.

parameters.label: Side  Group
parameters.name: sidegrp
parameters.description: Output group name to create for side bevel/extrude geometry.

parameters.label: This  SOP  is mainly used for generating bevels and extrusions of text where the input cross
parameters.description: sections are fed from a  Font SOP . Any curve or group of curves can also be used as input.

parameters.label: Offsets
parameters.description: This  SOP  can be used for generating two offsetting curves where the distance between the two curves remains constant. To do this, make sure that you set Side Mesh to No Output, the first thickness to zero and adjust the second to increase or decrease the distance of the offset.

parameters.label: Fixing Stray Normals
parameters.description: If your geometry contains normals that are pointed in many directions (say after reading geometry from a  File In SOP , or if you have a lot of open or non-planar polygons), you can fix it so that they are suitable for extrusion.

parameters.label: num_points
parameters.description: Number of points in this  SOP .

parameters.label: num_prims
parameters.description: Number of primitives in this  SOP .

parameters.label: num_particles
parameters.description: Number of particles in this  SOP .

parameters.label: last_vbo_update_time
parameters.description: Time spent in another thread updating geometry data on the  GPU  from the  SOP 's CPU data. As it is part of another thread, this time is not part of the usual frame time.

parameters.label: last_meta_vbo_update_time
parameters.description: Time spent in another thread updating meta surface geometry data (such as metaballs or nurbs) on the  GPU  from the  SOP 's CPU data. As it is part of another thread, this time is not part of the usual frame time.

parameters.label: total_cooks
parameters.description: Number of times the operator has cooked since the process started.

parameters.label: cook_time
parameters.description: Duration of the last cook in milliseconds.

parameters.label: cook_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the component timeline.

parameters.label: cook_abs_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the absolute time.

parameters.label: cook_start_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator started cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cook_end_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator finished cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cooked_this_frame
parameters.description: 1 if operator was cooked this frame.

parameters.label: warnings
parameters.description: Number of warnings in this operator if any.

parameters.label: errors
parameters.description: Number of errors in this operator if any.

parameters.label: The Graphics Processing Unit. This is the high
parameters.description: speed, many-core processor of the graphics card/chip that takes geometry, images and data from the CPU and creates images and processed data.
